paper_metadata.title: A Structured Survey of Quantum Computing for the Financial Industry

experiments.description: Theoretical gate-based quantum portfolio optimization for the unconstrained Markowitz minimum-risk portfolio problem using the HHL linear-systems approach.

algorithm.variant: Quantum computational finance portfolio optimization via HHL and variations

problem_formulation.objective_function: Identify the minimum-risk portfolio for a given desired return; the unconstrained Markowitz portfolio optimization is reduced to a linear least-squares problem.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No inequality constraints; no short-selling/budget constraints in the formulation described in the survey.

problem_instance.description: Unconstrained portfolio optimization under classical Markowitz theory.

speedup_claims.conditions: Unconstrained Markowitz portfolio optimization reduced to a linear least-squares problem; gate-based quantum computer using HHL and variations.
speedup_claims.caveats: Survey notes O(N) hardware requirements for storing/accessing data; practical speedup depends on data loading and problem assumptions.

experiments.description: Quantum annealing / hybrid solver portfolio optimization on a binary QUBO formulation for two stock indices.

algorithm.variant: D-Wave quantum annealer and hybrid solver for QUBO portfolio optimization

problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary portfolio optimization under Markowitz theory, selecting whether each asset is included or not.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Binary inclusion/exclusion only; QUBO formulation on a quantum annealer/hybrid solver.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: QUBO / Ising formulation (exact Hamiltonian not specified in the survey).

problem_instance.description: Optimal portfolio of two main stock indices.

speedup_claims.conditions: For the small example of two stock indices (Nikkei225 and S&P500) on a quantum annealer/hybrid solver.
speedup_claims.caveats: Survey does not report exact numerical performance values or a quantified speedup.

experiments.description: Reverse quantum annealing hybrid portfolio optimization on a QUBO formulation using real financial data statistics.

algorithm.variant: Reverse quantum annealing approach to portfolio optimization

problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary portfolio optimization formulated as QUBO.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Binary inclusion/exclusion formulation; reverse annealing used as a hybrid classical-quantum heuristic.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: QUBO / Ising formulation (exact Hamiltonian not specified in the survey).

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization using real financial data statistics; same general setting as the D-Wave portfolio optimization study.

dataset_specification.description: Real financial data statistics; exact assets and date range not specified in the survey.

speedup_claims.conditions: Reverse annealing protocol on real financial data statistics in a hybrid classical-quantum portfolio optimization setting.
speedup_claims.caveats: Survey states it is unclear what increase in speed could theoretically be achieved compared to a classical approach.

experiments.description: Quantum portfolio optimization under constraints by reducing Markowitz optimization to SOCPs and solving with a quantum interior-point method.

algorithm.variant: Quantum interior-point method for SOCPs applied to portfolio optimization

problem_formulation.objective_function: Constrained Markowitz portfolio optimization with positive portfolio weights and budget constraints, reduced to a second-order cone program (SOCP).
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Explicit inequality constraints handled by SOCP formulation.

problem_instance.description: Positive portfolio optimization with budget constraints.

speedup_claims.conditions: Constrained Markowitz portfolio optimization reduced to SOCP and solved with a quantum interior-point method.

experiments.description: Quantum portfolio rebalancing experiments using QAOA and the quantum alternating operator ansatz on an ideal simulator.

algorithm.variant: Portfolio rebalancing with soft constraints using QAOA; hard-constraint variant using the quantum alternating operator ansatz

problem_formulation.objective_function: Discrete portfolio rebalancing / optimization under constraints.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Soft constraints for the QAOA formulation; hard constraints for the quantum alternating operator ansatz.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Ising/QUBO-style formulation implied by the rebalancing problem.

problem_instance.description: Discrete portfolio rebalancing for institutional investors.
problem_instance.classical_preprocessing: Input data scaling is highlighted as important for the QAOA approach.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Scaling of input data for the QAOA approach.

results.value: quantum alternating operator approach outperforms QUAO

speedup_claims.factor: performance advantage over QUAO; no quantified speedup
speedup_claims.conditions: Ideal simulator experiments for discrete portfolio rebalancing; importance of input-data scaling noted.
speedup_claims.caveats: Further investigation needed; theoretical quantum advantage not yet clear.

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical optimization for index tracking using variational quantum algorithms (QAOA and VQE) in numerical simulation.

algorithm.variant: Hybrid quantum-classical optimization for index tracking with QAOA and VQE

problem_formulation.objective_function: Index tracking: select a subset of assets so the portfolio return is as close as possible to a reference index.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Cardinality constraints handled in a hybrid quantum-classical optimization framework.

problem_instance.description: Index tracking problem for portfolio selection.

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical mixed-binary optimization for transaction settlement, demonstrated on cloud-based quantum hardware.

algorithm.variant: Quantum algorithms for mixed binary optimization applied to transaction settlement using VQE and QAOA-style variational forms

problem_formulation.objective_function: Settle as many transactions as possible and/or maximize the total value of settled transactions.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Mixed binary optimization with discrete and continuous variables and inequality constraints handled by hybrid quantum/classical heuristics.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Binary quadratic / mixed-binary optimization formulation (exact Hamiltonian not specified in the survey).

experiments.description: Quantum amplitude estimation for Monte Carlo pricing of financial derivatives on a gate-based quantum computer.

algorithm.variant: Quantum amplitude estimation for derivative pricing

problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate derivative prices by preparing probability distributions in superposition and extracting expected payoff via amplitude estimation.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No explicit constraints described in the survey summary.

problem_instance.description: Pricing financial derivatives under the Black-Scholes-Merton setting.

dataset_specification.description: Black-Scholes-Merton model; exact derivative types not specified in the survey summary.

speedup_claims.conditions: Derivative pricing via quantum amplitude estimation on a gate-based quantum computer.
speedup_claims.caveats: Theoretical result; practical speedup depends on hardware and state-preparation costs.

experiments.description: Gate-based quantum option pricing experiments with error mitigation on a real quantum device, extending amplitude-estimation-based pricing circuits.

algorithm.variant: Option pricing using quantum computers with simple error mitigation

problem_formulation.objective_function: Price vanilla, multi-asset, barrier, and path-dependent options using amplitude estimation circuits.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Error mitigation applied to measurement/circuit errors; no optimization constraints described.

problem_instance.description: Pricing vanilla options, multi-asset options, barrier options, and path-dependent options.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Error mitigation reduced the average pricing error from 62% to 21% over the initial spot price.

speedup_claims.conditions: Error mitigation on a real quantum device for option pricing circuits.
speedup_claims.caveats: Survey reports error reduction, not a quantified speedup.

experiments.description: Quantum principal component analysis for pricing interest-rate derivatives under the Heath-Jarrow-Morton model on IBM quantum hardware.

algorithm.variant: Quantum principal component analysis (qPCA) for HJM factor reduction

problem_formulation.objective_function: Reduce the number of stochastic factors in the Heath-Jarrow-Morton model to price interest-rate derivatives.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No explicit constraints described in the survey summary.

problem_instance.description: Interest-rate derivative pricing with the multi-factor Heath-Jarrow-Morton model.

dataset_specification.description: Heath-Jarrow-Morton model; factor selection via PCA/qPCA.

experiments.description: Quantum amplitude estimation for VaR and CVaR risk analysis on a gate-based quantum computer, including a small two-asset hardware demonstration.

algorithm.variant: Quantum risk analysis using amplitude estimation

problem_formulation.objective_function: Evaluate Value-at-Risk (VaR) and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) from a portfolio loss distribution.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No explicit constraints described in the survey summary.

problem_instance.description: Risk analysis for a portfolio of two assets in the hardware demonstration.

dataset_specification.description: Two-asset example; no nonlinear payoff structures considered in the hardware demo.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical Monte Carlo / classical risk estimation
speedup_claims.conditions: VaR and CVaR estimation using quantum amplitude estimation on a gate-based quantum computer.
speedup_claims.caveats: Hardware demonstration is described as very low complexity; no nonlinear payoff structures considered.

experiments.description: Quantum amplitude estimation for credit risk analysis on a gate-based quantum computer.

algorithm.variant: Credit risk analysis using quantum amplitude estimation

problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No explicit constraints described in the survey summary.

speedup_claims.conditions: Credit risk analysis using quantum amplitude estimation on a gate-based quantum computer.
speedup_claims.caveats: Survey provides no numerical benchmark values.
